# Tacto Negotiation Arena - starter kit

A Python client for the arena API, two example buyer agents that negotiate by e-mail, helpers that
read the suppliers' documents and price a term sheet, a runner that plays many cases in parallel,
`arena-sim` - a local simulator of the arena's API - and a read-only MCP server over the data
package. Read the brief first
(`../brief/brief.md`); the full API is in `../brief/api.md`. Code: MIT.

## Quickstart - first agent on the board in 15 minutes

You need Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

**1. Get your team's key** (one per team): open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a
contact e-mail, and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once an organiser approves,
the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page (or its
link) shows it; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it. Keep it out of git.

```bash
cd starter-kit
uv sync --all-extras            # 2. install
cp .env.example .env            # 3. put ARENA_URL and your key (ARENA_API_KEY) into .env
uv run arena me                 # 4. your team and its practice quota
uv run arena cases              # 5. the practice cases (the 10 hosted ones are playable)
uv run arena play case:P01 -v   # 6. the naive agent negotiates one case
uv run arena board              # 7. you are on the practice leaderboard
```

Is the arena up? `curl $ARENA_URL/health`.

Step 6 prints the deal, your total cost `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the case score,
and a **replay link**: every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move, in words. That is
the learning loop - play a practice case, read the replay, improve your agent, play
again. In practice your best score per case counts, so play a case again whenever your agent improves.
**Quota:** 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours. `arena play` and `arena run` print
how many are left; `arena run` plays only the hosted practice cases and stops starting new ones
once the quota is used up (a `429` there does not go away by retrying). Plan your runs.

**Now the LLM agent.** Download the data (`ARENA_DATA=data/package` in `.env`), choose a model in
`.env` (your own key), then:

```bash
uv run arena data                                          # unpacks data/package (and the Sunday release once public)
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v
uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8   # every hosted practice case, 8 at a time
uv run arena play case:D02 -v                              # the sandbox: 3 demo suppliers, no board
```

**Sunday 08:00:** run `arena data` again - it adds `data/release-sunday` (new news, letters, a
memo). `DataPackage` merges its facts and documents automatically; hidden cases may cite them.

## Hello World (local, 3 commands)

No key yet? Play a whole case against the local simulator - no network, no quota, no LLM costs.
The simulator's supplier is a plain script; the real ones are on arena.tacto.ai. After
`uv sync --all-extras` (step 2 above):

```bash
# terminal 1: the simulator (--data is optional: leave it out until you have run `arena data`)
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package
# terminal 2: a simulator key, then the naive agent plays case:S01
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Hello World" sim                  # prints an api_key
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 ARENA_API_KEY=<the api_key> uv run arena play case:S01 -v
```

It prints the deal, `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the score and a replay link - open it
in your browser: the result on top, then every e-mail of the negotiation.

## Try it by hand (Postman, curl)

Feel the API before you put a model in front of it. On the real arena (practice and sandbox) the
60-second rule applies: three late replies in a row end the thread - too fast for typing. **By
hand, use the simulator first**, without the clock:

```bash
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package           # data/package from `arena data`; --data is optional
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # prints a simulator api_key
export SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8000 KEY=<the api_key>
```

Every call sends `X-API-Key: <key>`; every `POST` also `Content-Type: application/json` and a
fresh `X-Move-Id` (any unique string - the same id again returns the same answer). In Postman:
those headers, the body as raw JSON.

```bash
# 1. the cases: case:S01 has one supplier, sup:70270, and the negotiable fields unit_price, payment_days
curl -s "$SIM/v1/cases?set=practice" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"

# 2. open a session: the reply carries session_id (sim1 on a fresh simulator) and each supplier's quote e-mail
curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Move-Id: open-1" -d '{"case_id": "case:S01"}'

# 3. the supplier's opening e-mail: its term sheet (offer:70270-0) and the quote PDF to fetch
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"

# 4. your e-mail with an offer: the reply is the supplier's answer (status, term_sheets, claim_results)
curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270/messages" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Move-Id: msg-1" \
  -d '{"message": {"subject": "Adapter piece HI", "body": "Thank you for your quote. We offer 15.50 EUR at 60 days.",
       "term_sheets": [{"terms": {"unit_price": 15.5, "payment_days": 60}}]}}'

# 5. read the reply in the thread, and the session state
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

To close, send `{"message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:70270-1"}}}` (the
term sheet you take) or `{"message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}` to the same `messages` path;
the answer carries the result and score. The quote PDF: `GET $SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/attachments/att:70270-0-quote`.
The same calls work on the arena (`https://arena.tacto.ai`, your team's key, a practice case) - with
the clock running.

## The Live Final: waves, in parallel, within the cap

The final comes in 5 themed waves. A wave holds several hidden cases that appear when the host
starts it; play them all in parallel (up to 10 open sessions per key). Each wave has a hard
cap - **8 minutes** (the host may extend one) - and what is still open then ends without a deal.
Start the runner before the first wave and leave it running:

```bash
uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10
```

It polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`, plays every case of a new wave at once (one agent per case),
closes each case **90 seconds before its wave's cap** (read from the wave's `seconds_left`, so an
extension counts) - earlier if a round in that case took longer
(`play.closing_move`: the cheapest standing term
sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats your alternative, else walk away) and stops after the
fifth wave has closed. If it crashes, start it again: it picks up the sessions it had started.
In Python: `play_waves(client, new_agent)`. It reads only your own cases and sessions - during
the final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the screen or the event feed (`arena board`
is for you, not for the agent).

A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute; its time never counts against your 60 seconds,
and the client waits up to 180 seconds for a reply. The client paces itself below the
limit of 10 calls per second and retries dropped connections with the same `X-Move-Id`, so a
retry never sends a message twice. Rehearse with `arena run --set practice --parallel 10` (it counts against your quota) before
Sunday, from the machine and network you will use: every case should end well inside 8 minutes.

## Your own agent

An agent is any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": …, "message": {…}}`.
`threads` holds every e-mail so far per supplier, oldest first; supplier attachments come with
their text under `"text"`. The message is an e-mail - subject, body, up to 3 term sheets - or an
action that closes the case:

```python
from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, complete_offer, play, total_cost
from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
from arena_kit.play import latest, live_threads, standing


class Haggler:
    def decide(self, case, threads):
        sid = live_threads(threads)[0]
        events = threads[sid]
        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)  # the supplier's standing term sheet
        std = standard_terms(events)  # from its quote PDF: what closes if a field is missing
        if latest(events)["status"] in ("agreed", "final_offer"):
            return {
                "supplier_id": sid,
                "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
            }
        ask = complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": terms["unit_price"] * 0.97})
        print("their C:", total_cost(case, terms, std), "ours:", total_cost(case, ask))
        return {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {
                "subject": case["title"],
                "body": "Thank you for your quote. Could you send us a cost breakdown?",
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": ask}],
            },
        }


print(play(RemoteTable(ArenaClient()), "case:P01", Haggler()))
```

| Module | What |
|---|---|
| `client.py` | `ArenaClient`: one method per endpoint (messages, threads, attachments, back office, `me`, ...); paced, safe retries; `practice_remaining` |
| `play.py` | `play()`, `play_all()`, `play_waves()` (the Live Final); `RemoteTable` - the hosted arena (practice, sandbox, final) |
| `cost.py` | the published cost function C with the category goal's rates, `supplier_value` for the relationship term, must-haves, term-sheet completion |
| `docs.py` | supplier documents to text (PDF, XLSX); a quote PDF to its offered, standard and fixed terms |
| `data.py` | the data package and the Sunday release: `facts.json`, read-only SQL, lookup by ID, documents, cases |
| `agents/naive.py` | anchors 10 % low, splits the difference, accepts early - the baseline |
| `agents/llm.py` | the model writes the e-mail and the term sheets from the case and the data it points to; code computes C, reads the documents, removes IDs that do not exist, and refuses bad accepts |
| `sim.py` | `arena-sim`: the public API on your machine, with one plain scripted supplier (below) |
| `mcp_server.py` | the MCP server below |

The LLM agent is a starting point, not a winner: it sees only what the case file points to.
Finding the data that moves a supplier is your job - the worked example below shows one way for
one kind of argument. Ideas beyond it: mine the notes and e-mails, read the suppliers' signals and
documents, send two or three term sheets to learn what a supplier values, ask its roles the right
questions, keep RFQ threads alive in parallel, and never leak urgency, a budget or a missing
alternative.

**Strategic and bottleneck cases** (`category_goal` `stabilise` or `secure_supply`) charge C for a
deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin. Pass your estimate of the supplier to
price it - without one, `total_cost` leaves the term out:

```python
supplier = {"full_cost": 128.0, "interest_rate": 0.12, "standard": std}  # your estimate
total_cost(case, terms, std, supplier)
```

## Worked example: cite an index (case P01)

Brandlhuber, a foundry, announces +9.5 % on volute casings and blames energy and wages. Does the
data agree? `DataPackage` reads the package (the MCP server below gives an LLM the same access):

```python
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

pkg = DataPackage("data/package")
# 1. What drives this part's cost? The category team's estimate:
pkg.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = 'part:310010'")
# -> PPI-C241 (iron and steel) 0.26, PPI-D351 (electric power) 0.06, LCI-C (labour) 0.32
# 2. The letter blames energy: read the electricity producer price index for the last year.
rows = pkg.query(
    "SELECT id, month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-D351' AND month >= '2025-08' ORDER BY month"
)
# 3. Compute the change yourself - two months of one series, at most 12 months apart,
#    ending within the last 12 months of the data.
a, b = rows[0], rows[-1]
change = (b["value"] / a["value"] - 1) * 100
# 4. One sentence: the figure next to both IDs.
print(f"Electricity producer prices changed {change:+.1f}% from {a['month']} to {b['month']} ({a['id']}, {b['id']}).")
# -> Electricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08
#    (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).
```

Put that sentence into your e-mail and read `claim_results` in the reply: `verified` (the figure
matches the data), `irrelevant` (true, but not about this supplier's costs, or the window is too
old) or `contradicted` (a wrong figure - it costs trust). Whether it moves the price, and how far,
is the supplier's business - a true figure may disarm one supplier and leave the next cold; the
replay shows what it made of it. Which series matter to which
supplier, which window, and what else in the data speaks for you - that is up to your agent.

## Choosing a model

`LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` uses the Anthropic SDK (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` talks
to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY`) - OpenAI, Mistral, Groq, a local
Ollama (`http://localhost:11434/v1`) and many more. Or pass your own `complete(system, user) -> str`
to `LLMAgent`. Each message must arrive within **60 seconds** of the supplier's reply: prefer a
fast model or low effort, and do heavy research before you open a session. If the model fails or times out, the agent falls
back to the naive move instead of losing the case.

## Offline: arena-sim, the contract simulator

```bash
uv run arena-sim serve --data /path/to/data/package   # http://127.0.0.1:8000, event code "sim"
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # a simulator key
```

`arena register` exists for the simulator only: it hands out its own keys, which work nowhere
else. The arena's key comes from `/apply` (step 1).

`arena-sim` speaks the arena's public API exactly - paths, fields, statuses, error codes, limits,
the 60-second rule, quote PDFs and cost-breakdown XLSX files in the arena's format, RFQs with
parallel threads, leaderboard and replay JSON - with three example cases (`case:S01`-`S03`). Point
your agent at it to get the plumbing right without a network or a rate limit to worry about.
`--no-clock` switches the 60-second rule off for trying it by hand (above); without it the clock
runs, as on the arena. The first line it prints says which.

Its supplier is a deliberately plain script and **not** how the arena's suppliers behave: it opens
10 % above your current price, concedes a fixed 2 % per term sheet down to 90 %, agrees when you
meet its price, sends a final offer from round 5 and walks if you push after that; cited data is
only checked for existence. **The simulator teaches the contract; the real suppliers think for
themselves** - practise against them in the hosted arena and its sandbox (`--set sandbox`). We
don't hand out our suppliers: for a local opponent, build your own supplier simulator from the
public data - how would a foundry owner with a full order book answer your e-mail?
`starter-kit/Dockerfile` runs the simulator as a container. `uv run pytest` runs the kit's contract
tests against it; set `ARENA_TEST_URL` and `ARENA_TEST_KEY` to run them against a hosted arena too.

## MCP server over the data

A local, read-only MCP server (stdio) lets an MCP-capable agent or chat client explore the data
package itself. Six tools: `list_tables`, `query` (SELECT only, max 200 rows), `lookup` (the fact
behind a citable ID), `list_ids` (e.g. every month of one index series), `read_document`,
`get_case`.

```bash
uv run arena mcp --data /path/to/data/package   # speaks MCP on stdin/stdout
```

Add it to a client, e.g. Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add arena-data -- uv run --directory /path/to/starter-kit arena mcp --data /path/to/data/package
```

or any client with an `mcpServers` config:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"arena-data": {"command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--directory", "/path/to/starter-kit",
  "arena", "mcp", "--data", "/path/to/data/package"]}}}
```

## Run log: every negotiation on disk

Every `arena` command writes a folder under `starter-kit/logs/` (git-ignored), and so does every
`play()` from your own script. Each case played gets a folder with all of it in it: the e-mails,
what the agent decided and why, and every API call:

```
logs/
  index.jsonl                       one line per case: when, case, session, deal, score, folder
  2026-10-10_143205_play_case-P01/  one folder per command
    run.json  run.log  output.txt   command, git commit, model, how it ended; full DEBUG log; what it printed
    case-P01/
      transcript.md                 the e-mail discussion, readable: bodies, term sheets, claim results, result, back office
      session.json                  case file, every thread, result, session state
      decisions.jsonl  llm.jsonl    every move chosen; every model call (prompt, raw reply, what was sent)
      http.jsonl                    every API call: request, response, status, ms (never the key)
      attachments/                  quote PDFs and XLSX as received
```

```bash
uv run arena logs                 # the last 20 cases: deal, score, folder
uv run arena logs case:P01        # the latest transcript of that case (or pass a session id)
```

`ARENA_LOG_DIR` puts the logs elsewhere; `ARENA_LOG=0` switches them off.

## Good to know

- **60 s per message**, per thread. A late message counts as a timeout (your last offer repeated);
  `play()` reads the supplier's answer and goes on.
- **Invalid messages cost nothing**: `422` and no round used. `409` means the thread or case has
  ended, or you were late.
- **Your key is your team's.** Keep `.env` out of git.
- Tests: `uv run pytest`. Lint: `uv run ruff check .`

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
- no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - API v1

The arena speaks JSON over HTTPS. Base URL: `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1`. Every call except `/v1/data`, `/health` and
the leaderboards needs your team's key in the header `X-API-Key`. The starter kit wraps all of this in
`arena_kit.ArenaClient`. To try the API on your laptop, run `arena-sim` from the starter kit: the
same API with one plain scripted supplier - it teaches the contract, not the suppliers.

**Safe retries:** send a fresh `X-Move-Id` header (any unique string) with every `POST`. If the
network drops, repeat the request with the same `X-Move-Id`: the arena returns the answer it
already gave instead of acting twice. Reusing an id for a different request is a `422`. A request
body may be at most 64 KB.

Contents: [Flow](#flow) · [Endpoints](#endpoints) · [Messages](#messages) ·
[What counts](#what-counts) · [Documents](#documents) · [Terms](#terms) ·
[Case file](#case-file) · [Data IDs](#data-ids) ·
[Result](#result-trace-and-back-office) · [Cost and score](#cost-and-score) ·
[Live Final](#live-final-in-waves) · [Time, errors, limits](#time-errors-and-limits)

## Flow

```
GET  /v1/data                                        the data downloads (no key)
GET  /v1/me                                          your team: practice quota, best scores
GET  /v1/cases?set=practice                          the case files you can play
POST /v1/sessions                                    open a case → every supplier's quote e-mail
POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages  your e-mail → the supplier's reply  (repeat)
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}  a document the supplier attached
POST …/messages with "action": accept | walk_away    close the case → result
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}                              state; after the end score and trace
```

## Endpoints

### Your key

One key per team - a licence. Get it on the page `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`: enter your team name and a
contact e-mail, show the match code the page displays at the Tacto desk, and once an organiser
approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page
(or its link) shows the key; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it (the old key stops at once).

Send the key as `X-API-Key` with every call. A missing or unknown key is a `401`; a paused or
revoked key gets `403 "this key is paused - ask the organisers"` (or `revoked`) on every call.
There is no self-registration: `POST /v1/register` answers `403 "licences are issued by the
organisers"` (`arena-sim` keeps its own, for the simulator only).

### `GET /v1/me`

Where your team stands:

```json
{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "status": "active",
 "practice": {"used": 37, "left": 163, "limit": 200, "resets_at": "2026-10-11T09:42:10+00:00"},
 "best": {"case:P01": 0.71, "case:P04": 0.55}}
```
`practice`: sessions used and left in the rolling 24 hours, and when the oldest of them ages out
(the next one frees up); `best`: your best score per hosted practice case.

### `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox|final`

A list of full [case files](#case-file), so you can prepare before you open a session.

| Set | Cases | Replay |
|---|---|---|
| `practice` | all practice case files, to study; the **10 hosted** ones carry `"hosted": true` and can be played any time within your quota (a session on another is `403 "case:P06 is not hosted for practice"`); your best score per hosted case counts | right after the case |
| `sandbox` | `case:D01` (a price increase) and `case:D02` (an RFQ with two suppliers): three demo suppliers to try things on; no leaderboard | right after the case |
| `final` | the hidden cases (`"set": "hidden"`), wave by wave - see [Live Final](#live-final-in-waves); `403` before the first wave | after the final |

The replay is the same team view in every set: the e-mails as sent, terms, statuses, claim
results, the supplier's reasons in words and the score - as a real supplier would tell you. No rule
names, no internal parameters, none of the supplier's hidden figures (shown as `…`).

### `POST /v1/sessions`

`{"case_id": "case:P01"}` opens a case. Every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once (round 0);
from now on the 60-second clock runs per thread.

| Response field | |
|---|---|
| `session_id` | use in all further calls |
| `case` | the case file |
| `threads` | `{supplier_id: [opening message]}` - each supplier's quote e-mail, quote PDF attached |
| `opening` | the same quotes in the structured form of the `/moves` path |

Practice: your best score per case counts; at most 10 sessions open at a time (`429`).
**Quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** Every practice session start
answers with the header `X-Practice-Remaining: <sessions left>`. At the limit: `429` with a detail
starting `practice limit:` that names `resets_at`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` and no `Retry-After` -
retrying does not help before then. Sandbox and final sessions do not count. Final: one session per team and case; a second is a `409` naming the running session -
pick it up again with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`.

### `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}/messages`

Body `{"message": Message}` (see [Messages](#messages)). Returns the supplier's reply, a Message.
With an `action`, it closes the case and returns the [result](#result-trace-and-back-office):
`{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:…"}` takes that supplier's standing term sheet;
`{"type": "walk_away"}` ends the case without a deal.

A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60
seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).

`422`: invalid message - nothing happens, no round is used (e.g. a term sheet without every
negotiable field, a value outside the allowed options, an unknown or stale `term_sheet_id`, more
than 3 term sheets). `409`: the thread or session has ended (in the final also at the wave's cap),
you reached the round limit (you may still accept), or your message came too late - it counted
as a timeout; `GET` the thread for the supplier's answer.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`

The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
"buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
after a crash.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}`

The file of a supplier attachment (`application/pdf`, xlsx, ...), rendered from the supplier's
data. See [Documents](#documents).

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`

The session state: `session_id`, `case_id`, `set`, `status` (`open` | `ended`), `end_reason`
(`accepted`, `walked_away`, `no_deal`, `timeout`, `wave_cap`, `window_closed`), `rounds`, `opening`, `threads`
(per supplier: `offer_id`, `status`, `offers`, `closed`, `seconds_left`) and, after the end,
`result` and `replay_url`.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/backoffice`

The supplier's roles talking internally (who asked whom, approvals, documents attached), in the
same team view: their words, without hidden figures or internal names. Only after the case has
ended - in the final after the final; before that `403`.

### Lists and boards

- `GET /health` - is the arena up? No key needed.
- `GET /v1/data` - the data downloads, no key needed: `{"package": {"url": "/v1/data/package.zip"},
  "release-sunday": {"public": false, "at": "2026-10-11T06:00:00+00:00"}}`. Once the Sunday
  release is public it carries `"url": "/v1/data/release-sunday.zip"` - new news, letters and a
  memo, with their own `facts.json` (new IDs only; package v1 stays as it is). Hidden cases may
  cite them; practice cases stay on package v1.

- `GET /v1/sessions?set=practice|sandbox|final` - your sessions: `session_id`, `case_id`, `status`,
  `end_reason`, `deal`, `score`, `rounds`, `created_at`.
- `GET /v1/leaderboard?set=practice|final` (JSON), `GET /leaderboard` (HTML screen) - no key
  needed. Practice: `total` = the mean of your best score per hosted case × 100 (cases not played
  count 0). Final: hidden cases only, live, as **points so far**:
  ```json
  {"set": "final", "cases": 6,
   "teams": [{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "played": 6, "deals": 6, "rounds": 21,
              "waves": {"1": 37.0, "2": 40.8}, "total": 77.8, "rank": 1,
              "saved_eur": 48210, "saved_eur_waves": {"1": 30115, "2": 18095}}],
   "waves": [{"n": 1, "theme": "Opening", "running": false, "closed": true, "seconds_left": 0}, …]}
  ```
  Per team, `waves` holds each started wave's score: the mean of its case scores × 100, 0-100, one
  decimal (a case you did not play scores your alternative once its wave has closed). `total` is
  the sum of those wave columns as shown - your points so far, up to 500 after five waves. Ranked by
  `total`; an exact tie goes to more `deals`, then fewer `rounds`. `cases` counts the cases of the
  waves started so far. **€ saved** (`saved_eur`, whole euros, per started wave in `saved_eur_waves`)
  is a side number and does not rank: per ended session `C_open − C_end`, where `C_end` is `c_deal`,
  or `c_alt` without a deal (0 if the case has no alternative) - money saved against the cheapest
  opening offer, over the case's horizon (`horizon_years`, 1-2 years), the same C as
  the score. It can be negative (a deal or an alternative dearer than the opening offer); a case
  you did not play saves nothing, nor does a deal that breaks a must-have (it scores 0). In the final the feed's `deal` and `no_deal` events carry it too.
  During the Live Final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the results, the screen or the
  event feed (`/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`, `/v1/results`, `/results`)
  - they are for people.
- `GET /v1/results` (JSON), `GET /results` (page) - no key needed: the final's standings for people,
  every team: the final leaderboard above plus `"replays": true` once the final is closed. Before
  the first wave: no teams, nothing about the plan. `GET /v1/results/{team_name}` - one team's cases
  of the **started** waves: per wave `n`, `theme`, `running`, `closed`, `points`, `saved_eur` and
  `cases` - `case_id`, `title`, `type`, `suppliers` (names), `status` (`not started`, `in play`,
  `deal`, `no deal`; `not played` once its wave has closed - it scores your alternative), `end_reason`,
  `score`, `saved_eur`, `rounds`, and after the final `replay_url`. Both cached for 5 seconds.
- `GET /live` - the build page, no key needed (Sat 10:00 - Sun 12:00): every team's quota use,
  practice records and highlights.
- `GET /replay/{sid}` (link in the session's `replay_url`): a finished negotiation step by step -
  every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move in words, the same view in every set.
  Play, read the replay, improve, play again: that is the learning loop. Final: after the final,

## What counts

**Term sheets bind** - nothing else. They are taken exactly as you send them, never guessed from
prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.

**Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
are context, not checks.

| You cite | Checked | Your figure |
|---|---|---|
| 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |
| a `quote` of this case (in its `refs` or your alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | its price, same part | EUR |
| `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
| 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |
| `fc` / `cost` / `news` | the recorded change / the estimate / that it is about this supplier | a % / EUR / - |
| a letter `doc` giving notice + the contract `ctr` | the notice the letter gives, against the contract's | days |

data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.

once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
supplier you cite it to.

and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,

**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unit_price` | number, € with 2 decimals, per the part's `price_unit` | price |
| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |

## Cost and score

With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:

```
years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
covered   = min(V, N) · years
pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
```

The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
expected move of the clause's series.

**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.

## Live Final in waves

The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
`GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
| `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
| `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |

Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
/v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
`GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
--set final` in the starter kit does this.

## Time, errors and limits

- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
  thread.
- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `401` | missing or unknown `X-API-Key` |
| `403` | paused or revoked key; a practice case that is not hosted; `POST /v1/register` (keys come from `/apply`); the final's case list before the first wave; a final case whose wave has ended; back office before the end |
| `404`

| `buyer` | your need and rates, below |
| `round_limit` | your messages per thread, default 10 |
| `refs` | data the case points to - a start, not the whole story |
| `facts` | hidden cases: facts that exist only in this case (e.g. a new letter), in the format of `facts.json`, citable in this case |

`buyer`:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `need_per_year`, `horizon_years` | the need the deal should cover, and over how many years (≤ 3) |
| `current_unit_price` | what you pay until a new price takes effect |
| `fallback_unit_price` | what uncovered need costs (re-tender or spot, incl. switching) |
| `interest_rate`, `reference_payment_days` | your cost of money per year; your standard payment term |
| `need_lead_time_days`, `late_cost_per_day` | the lead time you need; € per day beyond it |
| `cost_per_defect` | € per defective part |
| `category_goal` | `stabilise` (strategic), `secure_supply` (bottleneck), `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - the company's category strategy for this part; the briefing says it in words, and the rates in this block follow it |
| `fallback_risk_pct` | % added to what uncovered need costs: buying it later is a risk |
| `index_risk_pct` | % of the indexed spend: the risk you carry with an index clause |
| `sustainable_margin_pct`, `relationship_eur_per_point` | `stabilise` and `secure_supply` only: the margin a healthy supplier needs, and € per margin point and year that a deal leaves it below |
| `freight_eur_per_unit` | `{EXW, FCA, DAP}` |
| `index_paths` | `{series: change}` - the expected index move over the horizon, `0.04` = +4% |
| `must_haves` | `[{field, op, value}]`, `op` one of `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`; a deal that breaks one scores 0 |
| `alternative` | `{kind: none \| quote \| current_contract, ref, terms}` - what you get without a deal |

## Data IDs

IDs have the form `<type>:<id>[@period]`, are unique across the package and sit in the first
column of each table. `facts.json` in the package lists every citable ID with the values the arena
checks:

| ID | Fields |
|---|---|
| `idx:<series>@YYYY-MM` | `series`, `month`, `value` |
| `quote:` | `part`, `supplier`, `unit_price` (+ the quote's other terms) |
| `sc:<supplier>@YYYYQn` | `supplier`, `otd_pct`, `ppm` |
| `qn:` | `supplier`, `part`, `ppm` |
| `po:` | `supplier`, `part`, `unit_price` |
| `cost:<part>` | `part`, `unit_cost` |
| `fc:<part>@YYYY-MM` | `part`, `change_pct` |
| `news:` | `supplier` (or null) |
| `doc:` | `supplier`, `date`, `days` (notice given), `asked_price` (price letters) |
| `ctr:` | `supplier`, `days` (notice agreed) |

Offers made in the session are citable as `offer:` IDs.

content.text:
I'd restructure how the agent writes emails, not just tweak the prompt. Right now [llm.py](starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/llm.py) makes one model call that has to read the supplier, choose a strategy, pick the numbers and write the email all at once, and it only sees what the case file points to. Most of the gains will come from three things: what the agent knows about the supplier, letting code decide the numbers, and checking the email before it's sent.

## What's wrong today

1. **It can't see the supplier's history.** `prepare()` loads only the case's `refs`. Take P01 (Brandlhuber):
   - The owner works from his own index spreadsheet that's two years old (`20260824-70110-M1`), so real index data could actually change his mind.
   - He asked to be paid within 10 days in exchange for a cash discount (`20260902-70110-M2`). That's a trade we can offer.
   - He expects "partnership" (`20260715-70110-M5`), and the negotiation history shows he has repeatedly sold below his full cost.

   The agent sees none of this. These notes are where the brief says the edge is.
2. **The model invents prices and data figures.** It proposes term sheets freehand and works out the percentages in its own claims. A wrong figure comes back `contradicted` and costs trust. The guard only deletes unknown IDs, and that can leave a stray figure behind with no source.
3. **The text and the term sheets can disagree.** Nothing checks that the prices in the body match the term sheets attached to the email.
4. **Data citations are wasted.** Only 3 claims are checked per message, and each ID counts once per case. The agent doesn't track what it has already cited, doesn't use the `refs` field, and doesn't plan which argument to use in which round.
5. **It has short memory and no plan.** It sees the last 6 messages, each cut to 800 characters, and has no record of its own concessions or of what the supplier has already pushed back on.
6. **The tone is generic.** It writes "Dear Sir or Madam" to everyone. It doesn't address the person who actually replied, doesn't adjust to a family foundry vs. a corporate group, and doesn't answer the points the supplier raised.
7. **Nothing checks for leaks.** The "don't reveal urgency, budget or that we have no alternative" rule is only in the prompt. Nothing checks the finished text.
8. **Preparation happens on the clock.** `play()` opens the session (`play.py:160`) before `decide()` runs `prepare()`, so research eats into the 60-second limit per message.

## The plan

### Phase 1: A supplier profile, built before the clock starts (biggest lever)
New `arena_kit/dossier.py`. For each supplier in the case it pulls together, with an SQL query per source:
- correspondence for that supplier (call notes, meeting notes, letters) from `documents.csv` plus the files themselves;
- `negotiation_history`, i.e. how far they've given in on past asks;
- `supplier_intel`: owner type, equity ratio, change in credit score;
- scorecards, quality notifications, our past orders and quotes, news;
- the cost drivers and index series for the part.

One cheap model call per supplier, run before the session opens, turns that into a short **profile**:
- persona: who's at the desk and the tone they respond to;
- pressures: cash, capacity, energy costs;
- levers: payment days, volume, contract length, effective date;
- sore points: things to avoid;
- best arguments: ranked.

Cache it per supplier, so cases in the same wave share it. Change `play()` and `play_waves()` to call `agent.prepare(case)` before `table.open()`; the case file is already available from `GET /v1/cases`.

### Phase 2: Pre-checked arguments, built by code
New `arena_kit/claims.py`. For each supplier, code builds sentences ready to cite and checks each one against `facts.json` using the arena's own rules:
- index changes: one series, at most 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months, ±0.5 percentage points;
- rival quotes, our purchase-order prices, scorecard on-time delivery and defect rates (ppm), should-cost estimates, and notice period in a letter vs. the contract.

Each one gets its figure, its IDs, a "direction" (whether it helps or hurts us) and a relevance score. Example: `"Electricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08 (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08)."`

The model picks claims by key and they're inserted word for word, so it never computes a figure itself. Code tracks spent IDs per case, never sends more than 3 claims per message, and skips any argument the profile marks as one this supplier won't accept. Arguments that would help the supplier (e.g. an index that rose) are dropped.

### Phase 3: Code decides the offer, the model words it
Split each turn into two steps.
1. **Choose the move (code, using the profile).** A concession plan per thread, based on cost C:
   - open with a strong anchor;
   - concede in shrinking steps, never giving more than they last gave;
   - stop at the walk-away point (the alternative, or our cost limit).

   Then generate 2–3 term sheets that trade along different dimensions: price vs. payment days vs. effective date vs. volume. Each is checked with `total_cost` so they cost us about the same. That way, whichever one the supplier picks tells us what it values. Accept, walk away and push are also decided here, using `final_offer`, rounds left, and how far its last reply moved.
2. **Write the email (model).** The model gets the chosen move, the profile, the shortlist of checked claims, the supplier's last email in full, and a running summary of the negotiation. It returns `{subject, opening, claim_keys, question, closing}`. Code then assembles the email and writes the "Option A / Option B" paragraph itself from the actual term sheets, so text and numbers always match.

   If time is short, merge both steps into one call that returns both parts. The point is the split in responsibility, not the extra round trip.

### Phase 4: How the email itself is written (prompt rewrite)
- **Structure, about 120 words or less:**
  1. acknowledge their specific point by name;
  2. one or two data arguments, each in its own sentence;
  3. the options, presented as a choice ("Option A … or Option B …");
  4. one targeted question;
  5. a warm, professional close.
- **Address the person:** reply to the role that wrote (`from: sales@…`, the owner, finance) and keep the subject on `Re: <their subject>` so the thread stays together.
- **Respond to what they said:** if they defend a cost driver ("labour costs up 2.7%"), concede the true part and turn it into a trade. Don't repeat the argument they just rejected.
- **Match the tone to the persona:**
  - family firm: relationship and continuity, recognising past loyalty;
  - corporate group: give the rep something they can take to their boss for approval;
  - near-monopolist: security of volume and long-term planning;
  - job shop short of cash: lead with payment terms.
- **Make each question count, by round:**
  - round 1: ask for a cost breakdown (an open supplier sends an XLSX);
  - lead time and capacity in capacity cases;
  - an 8D report in quality cases;
  - cheaper engineering variants.
- **Never write:** deadlines, "we must", budgets, "we have no other option", internal C or fallback prices, must-have wording. Treat threats as a last resort, and only when we have a real alternative.
- **A few strong examples in the prompt:** one example email per case type (price increase, RFQ, renewal, quality, capacity), each written in the target style.

### Phase 5: Checks before sending (extend `guard()`)
Before an email goes out, the guard:
- re-checks every figure-plus-ID sentence against the facts locally, and drops any that fail;
- confirms every price and payment term in the body matches one of the term sheets;
- rejects leak phrases with a regex, and in borderline cases with a cheap model check;
- enforces the length limit, no placeholders (`[Name]`), and at most 3 claims;
- if a check fails, it repairs the email in code (rebuilds it from the parts) rather than falling back to the naive move.

### Phase 6: Memory across rounds
- Keep a per-thread state object: what we offered and they offered each round, claim results, arguments they rejected, questions they've answered, and documents received (cost breakdown → feed real cost lines back into the arguments).
- Pass that compact state instead of the last 6 raw messages. Always include the supplier's latest email in full.
- **RFQs:** cite the best rival quote to the other bidders (one citation per supplier is allowed). Keep the leader warm while squeezing the runner-up.

### Phase 7: Speed and model choice
- The current model is `gpt-4.1-mini` with a 45-second timeout. Measure p95 response time with the new prompt; the target is under 25 seconds per turn, including the request round trip.
- Use a stronger model (e.g. `claude-sonnet-5-5` / `claude-opus-5-5` at low effort) for the profiles, before the clock starts. Use a fast one for the in-round writing step.

### Phase 8: A loop to test improvements
- **Offline:** a "supplier critic" built from the profile that scores each draft email: does it answer their point, does it leak, does it use their lever. Also add unit tests for `claims.py` against `facts.json`, so nothing we send gets `contradicted`.
- **Practice (200 sessions a day):** play the 10 hosted cases in a fixed order. Read the replays for the supplier's stated reasons. Track per case: score, rounds, verified vs. contradicted claims, and number of fallbacks. Compare variants on the same cases. The new `runlog` / `arena logs` already captures what's needed.
- **Watch for a third of final cases being new combinations:** hold out 3 practice cases while tuning prompts, so we don't overfit to the practice suppliers.

## Order I'd build it in
1. **Phase 1 + moving `prepare()` before the session opens.** Biggest gain, low risk.
2. **Phase 2 (checked claims) + Phase 5 checks.** Removes the `contradicted` hits that cost trust.
3. **Phase 4 prompt rewrite with the profile.** Fast to iterate on with replays.
4. **Phase 3 code-driven offers + Phase 6 memory.** The biggest score gain, but the most work.
5. **Phases 7–8,** with ongoing practice runs.

There are no run logs in `starter-kit/logs/` yet. Before changing anything, I'd play the hosted practice set once with the current LLM agent to get a baseline score per case.

I can start on Phase 1 now, or publish this plan as a page you can share with your team.

import argparse
import functools
import io
import json
import logging
import os
import statistics
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from . import runlog
from .client import ArenaClient, ArenaError
from .play import RemoteTable, hosted, play, play_all, play_waves


def load_env(path=".env"):
    """Read KEY=VALUE lines from .env into the environment (real env vars win)."""
    p = Path(path)
    if p.is_file():
        for line in p.read_text().splitlines():
            key, sep, value = line.partition("=")
            value = value.strip().strip("\"'")
            if sep and value and not key.strip().startswith("#"):
                os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value)


def agent_factory(name, data):
    from .agents import LLMAgent, NaiveAgent, llm_from_env

    if name == "naive":
        return NaiveAgent
    package = None
    if data:
        from .data import DataPackage

        package = DataPackage(data)
        package.lookup("")  # build the ID index once, before agents share it
    complete = llm_from_env()
    return lambda: LLMAgent(complete, package)


def summary(result):
    keep = ("deal", "supplier_id", "terms", "c_open", "c_deal", "c_best", "score")
    return {k: result.get(k) for k in keep if k in result}


def show_logs(args):
    """Past negotiations from logs/index.jsonl, or one transcript."""
    index = runlog.log_root() / "index.jsonl"
    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in index.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()] if index.is_file() else []
    if not rows:
        return print(f"nothing logged yet in {runlog.log_root()}")
    if args.query:
        hits = [r for r in rows if any(args.query in str(r.get(k)) for k in ("case_id", "session_id", "path", "run"))]
        if not hits:
            raise SystemExit(f"no logged case matches {args.query!r}")
        transcript = runlog.log_root() / hits[-1]["path"] / "transcript.md"
        print(transcript.read_text())
        return print(f"({transcript})")
    for r in rows[-args.last :]:
        score = "-" if r.get("score") is None else f"{100 * r['score']:.1f}"
        deal = "error" if r.get("error") else ("deal" if r.get("deal") else "no deal")
        who = r.get("model") or r.get("agent") or ""
        print(f"{r['at'][:16]}  {r['case_id']:<10} {deal:<8} score {score:>5}  {who:<18} {r['path']}")
    print(f"\n{len(rows)} cases logged in {runlog.log_root()}; `arena logs <case or session>` prints a transcript")


def main(argv=None):
    load_env()
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="arena")
    ap.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
    verbose = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)  # -v also after the command
    verbose.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true", default=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser = functools.partial(sub.add_parser, parents=[verbose])
    r = sub.add_parser(
        "register", help="arena-sim only: get a simulator key (the arena's key comes from the organisers)"
    )
    r.add_argument("team_name")
    r.add_argument("event_code")
    data = {"default": os.environ.get("ARENA_DATA"), "help": "data package folder"}
    sets = {"default": "practice", "help": "practice, final or sandbox"}
    c = sub.add_parser("cases", help="list the cases you can play")
    c.add_argument("--set", **sets)
    p = sub.add_parser("play", help="play one case")
    p.add_argument("case_id")
    p.add_argument("--agent", default="naive", choices=["naive", "llm"])
    p.add_argument("--data", **data)
    a = sub.add_parser("run", help="play every case of a set in parallel")
    a.add_argument("--set", **sets)
    a.add_argument("--agent", default="naive", choices=["naive", "llm"])
    a.add_argument("--data", **data)
    a.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=8, help="cases at once (at most 10)")
    a.add_argument("--waves", type=int, default=5, help="final: stop after this many waves have closed")
    d = sub.add_parser("data", help="download and unpack the data (package, Sunday release once public)")
    d.add_argument("--out", default="data", help="folder to unpack into")
    sub.add_parser("me", help="your team: practice quota used and left, best score per case")
    b = sub.add_parser("board", help="show the leaderboard")
    b.add_argument("--set", **sets)
    m = sub.add_parser("mcp", help="run the read-only MCP server over the data (stdio)")
    m.add_argument("--data", **data)
    lg = sub.add_parser("logs", help="past negotiations from the run log, or one transcript")
    lg.add_argument("query", nargs="?", help="a case or session id (the latest match is shown)")
    lg.add_argument("--last", type=int, default=20, help="how many cases to list")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO if args.verbose else logging.WARNING,
        format="%(asctime)s %(message)s",
        datefmt="%H:%M:%S",
    )

    if args.cmd == "mcp":  # stdio belongs to the MCP protocol: no run log
        from .mcp_server import main as serve

        return serve(args.data)
    if args.cmd == "logs":
        return show_logs(args)
    label = {"play": lambda: f"play_{args.case_id}", "run": lambda: f"run_{args.set}_{args.agent}"}
    runlog.start_run(label.get(args.cmd, lambda: args.cmd)(), ["arena", *(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)])
    try:
        dispatch(args)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        runlog.end_run("interrupted")
        raise
    except BaseException as e:
        failed = not isinstance(e, SystemExit) or e.code not in (None, 0)
        if failed and not isinstance(e, SystemExit):
            logging.getLogger("arena").exception("arena %s failed", args.cmd)
        runlog.end_run("error" if failed else "ok", f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}" if failed else None)
        raise
    runlog.end_run()


def dispatch(args):
    client = ArenaClient()
    if args.cmd == "register":
        out = client.register(args.team_name, args.event_code)
        print(json.dumps(out, indent=2))
        print("\nA simulator key: put it into .env as ARENA_API_KEY=... while you point ARENA_URL at arena-sim.")
    elif args.cmd == "cases":
        cases = client.cases(args.set)
        playable = {c["case_id"] for c in hosted(cases)}
        for case in cases:
            mark = "" if case["case_id"] in playable else "  (not hosted: data only)"
            print(case["case_id"], case.get("type", ""), case.get("title", "") + mark, sep="  ")
    elif args.cmd == "me":
        try:
            print(json.dumps(client.me(), indent=2))
        except ArenaError as e:
            print(f"no team view on this arena ({e})" if e.status == 404 else e)
    elif args.cmd == "board":
        print(json.dumps(client.leaderboard(args.set), indent=2))
    elif args.cmd == "data":
        for name, info in client.downloads().items():
            if info.get("url"):
                zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(client.download(name))).extractall(args.out)
                print(f"{name}: {Path(args.out) / name}")
            else:
                print(f"{name}: public from {info.get('at')}")
    elif args.cmd == "play":
        table = RemoteTable(client)
        try:
            result = play(table, args.case_id, agent_factory(args.agent, args.data)())
        except ArenaError as e:  # e.g. not hosted, the quota, a paused key: the arena says why
            raise SystemExit(str(e)) from None
        print(json.dumps(summary(result), indent=2))
        replay = client.session(table.session_id).get("replay_url")
        if replay:  # the supplier's reasons, move by move: read it, improve, play again
            print(f"replay: {os.environ['ARENA_URL'].rstrip('/')}{replay}")
    elif args.set == "final":  # waits for each wave and plays its cases within the cap
        out = play_waves(client, agent_factory(args.agent, args.data), args.waves, min(args.parallel, 10))
    else:
        ids = [case["case_id"] for case in hosted(client.cases(args.set))]
        out = play_all(
            lambda: RemoteTable(client),
            ids,
            agent_factory(args.agent, args.data),
            min(args.parallel, 10),
        )
    if args.cmd == "run":
        for case_id, result in out.items():
            print(case_id, result if isinstance(result, Exception) else summary(result))
        scores = {c: r.get("score") for c, r in out.items() if isinstance(r, dict)}
        if args.set == "final" and scores:  # points so far: each wave 0-100, their sum, as the board counts
            waves = {}
            for case in client.cases("final"):  # your own case list: which wave each case was in
                waves.setdefault(case["wave"], []).append(scores.get(case["case_id"]) or 0)
            points = {n: round(100 * statistics.mean(v), 1) for n, v in sorted(waves.items())}
            print(f"waves: {points}  points so far: {round(sum(points.values()), 1)} (the board is the record)")
        elif scores and all(v is not None for v in scores.values()):
            print(f"mean score: {100 * statistics.mean(scores.values()):.1f}")
    if args.cmd in ("play", "run") and client.practice_remaining is not None:
        print(f"practice sessions left today: {client.practice_remaining}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    def _tick(self, s):
        """The 60-second rule: a supplier left waiting counts a timeout - its offer stands; the
        third in a row (or one after the last round) ends the thread. Returns who just got one."""
        late = set()
        if self.no_clock:
            return late
        for sup, th in s["threads"].items():
            while s["status"] == "open" and not th["closed"] and self.clock() > th["last_at"] + MOVE_S:
                th["last_at"] += MOVE_S
                th["round"] += 1
                th["timeouts"] += 1
                th["late"].append({"offer_id": th["offer_id"], "status": th["status"], "terms": th["stated"]})
                if th["timeouts"] >= 3 or th["round"] >= s["case"]["round_limit"]:
                    th["closed"] = "timeout"
                late.add(sup)
        self._settle(s, "timeout")
        return late

## Time, errors and limits

- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
  thread.
- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `401` | missing or unknown `X-API-Key` |
| `403` | paused or revoked key; a practice case that is not hosted; `POST /v1/register` (keys come from `/apply`); the final's case list before the first wave; a final case whose wave has ended; back office before the end |
| `404` | unknown case (including a final case whose wave has not started), session, thread or attachment |
| `409` | thread or session ended (also at a wave's cap); round limit reached; late (timeout); final case already played |
| `413` | request body over 64 KB |
| `422` | invalid request or message - nothing happens, no round is used |
| `429` | over a limit: calls per second (`Retry-After: 1` - retry), open sessions (close one first), the practice quota (`practice limit: …`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` - wait until `resets_at`) |

Errors carry a readable reason: `{"detail": "…"}`.

"""What the data says about one supplier: the dossier code gathers before a case opens.

The case file points to a handful of facts; the supplier's real situation sits in the rest of the
package - call and meeting notes, letters, past negotiations, its financials, our payment record,
its scorecards, the cost structure of the part. `gather` collects all of it for one supplier and
the case's parts, `render` turns it into text a language model reads once, before the clock runs.
Built on `DataPackage`, so the Sunday release is included.
"""

    re.I,
)
